# Items from other projects (insert, links)

Any project in the folder can give items to this one: the whole project, or any top-level parts, assemblies, sub-assemblies (picked from inside an assembly), components, boards, schematics, parameter sets, sheets or sketches. Reuse instead of redrawing: "put the ESP32 board from esp32-board in this case" is an insert, not a rebuild.

- `./ise insert --from <project> --list` shows the source's items as a tree (kind, what each brings, ids). Pick by name or id: `./ise insert --from esp32-board "ESP32 USB-C board"`; several at once; `--all` for the whole project. `--dry-run` says what would come (counts by kind, names it would rename, materials already here) without inserting.
- Everything an item needs comes with it, consistently: the definitions and programs it uses (and the files they read, by content hash), materials, parameter sets its formulas read, stock items, an assembly's instances, joints, couplings, poses and requirements on it, configurations, a board's components, tracks, vias, zones and 3D model (and the library footprints and symbols it names), a schematic with its board. Things that only share a material with it stay behind. Every id is new and every reference rewritten, so inserting twice, or from two projects, never collides; it is one change (one undo).
- Linked (the default) follows the source: `./ise links` lists each link (from where, what, at which source revision) and whether it is up to date or has an update available (how many new, changed, removed); `./ise links update [id]` takes the source's changes (one undoable change); `--auto` at insert or `./ise links auto <id> on` makes it take them by itself as soon as the source changes (while the engine runs; when the engine starts, every project's links are checked at once: automatic ones catch up with what changed while it was off, the others show "update available"). Where the item is placed here, and names changed here to avoid a clash, stay as they are here; edits made here to something the source did not change stay; where both changed the same thing the source wins and the update says so. Deleted here stays deleted. `./ise links break <id>` (the link, or any item it brought) makes the items an ordinary local copy. `--copy` at insert makes that copy straight away.
- Linked items are read-only here, as their source made them (like a linked component in other CAD): a command that changes one is refused with `LINKED_READ_ONLY` and says what to do. Where an item is placed (a top-level instance's position, rotation, name and parent; a placed part's x, y, z) stays yours to change, and removing one is allowed. To change what it is: change it in the source project and update; or `./ise links local <id> on` ("Edit locally": edits here are allowed, and updates merge the source's changes with them, the source's winning where both changed the same thing; `off` makes it read-only again); or `./ise links break <id>` to make it your own copy. Ask the person which they want before breaking a link.
- Placement: by default things land where they are in the source; `--origin` puts the first picked item's origin at this project's origin, `--at x,y,z` (mm) at that point. A sub-assembly or component picked from inside an assembly gets its own top-level instance, where it sat in the whole source assembly.
- A definition whose name is taken here (two "Bracket"s) is renamed "Bracket (<source title>)", and the insert prints each rename; identical materials (and library parts) already here are used rather than copied. Stock items keep their catalogue names.
- The person does the same from Components › Insert from project (or the project menu): pick the project, tick items in its tree (search filters it), choose Linked or Copy and where it goes (same place, origin, or click a point in the view). Linked items show a link badge in the Components tree and Properties with "up to date" / "update available", Update, Update automatically, Edit locally and Break link; while a link is read-only, its items' fields in Properties are greyed out with the reason.
